This is affecting our checkout / fraud scoring pipeline (batch size 64). We have partial mitigation by dropping concurrency, but SLA breaches are imminent.

Attached is a short KPI snapshot and the recent node allocation report. We are on Redwood Private (v2.3.1) with kernel opts set to default. Please treat as P0 and advise immediate next steps; we will need an exec-level fallback plan if this can't be resolved in the hour.

- Alex Rivera, Head of Platform (Auric Systems)

Thanks — initial findings from the remote diagnostics:

- Node telemetry: CPU and GPU utilization per-shard look normal; memory pressure on the request workers is elevated and GC cycles are increased on a subset of nodes (3/12). No OOMs reported yet.
- Transport: intermittent increased latency on the intra-cluster fabric correlating with p95 spikes. Packet retransmits visible on two hosts — likely network path flaps with our kernel's default congestion settings.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~28% when the p95 spike started; cache evictions increased. This aligns with the batch-processing threads starving for KV responses.

Quick mitigation plan (can be performed in 30-45 minutes):
1) Apply a conservative kernel tuning patch (tcp_rmem/tcp_wmem and net.core.netdev_max_backlog) to reduce retransmit sensitivity and increase socket buffers on affected hosts. Patch attached as a short proposal (kernel-tuning-proposal.pdf).
2) Temporarily lower per-shard concurrency from 64 -> 32 for the fraud scoring route to reduce KV contention.
3) Enable a short-lived prefix cache on the largest model endpoints to reduce KV lookups for repeated tokens.
4) Prepare routing rule in Redwood Console to direct 20% of traffic to hosted fallback in us-west region as a safety net; require signed approval from Auric.

Risks: kernel tweaks need a rolling restart of affected hosts; we can stagger to avoid full outage. Prefix cache may slightly increase latency for cold requests but will reduce backend load.

I recommend we start 1+2 immediately and keep hosted fallback on standby. I’ll coordinate with infra to stage the kernel roll.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <arivera@auricsys.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RED: sudden private cluster throughput collapse (p95 spikes, 5xx) — plan and exec ask

Alex — quick update and ask for sign-off.

What we've done (in the last 18 hours):
- Rolled a conservative kernel tuning patch to the 3 most-impacted hosts during a 15-minute rolling window. Observed immediate reduction in retransmit counts and p95 improvement from ~1.6s -> ~420ms on those hosts.
- Reduced concurrency for the fraud scoring route from 64 -> 32; overall throughput dropped ~18% but error rate dropped under 0.8%.
- Enabled prefix caching on the high-volume endpoints; cache hit-rate climbed to ~62% on subsequent loads.
- Kept hosted fallback staged but not enabled; we prepared a routing policy to route 20% traffic if requested.

Ask / exec items:
- Auric execs: please approve a 30-minute sandboxed fallback window to our hosted cluster (we will route only low-risk traffic paths) to completely avoid SLA breaches while we complete a full rolling kernel update across the fleet. This requires sign-off by Aurora Ops + Security.
- Redwood leadership: Markus — can you prepare a short exec note for our CRO and CTO (1 slide) summarizing impact, credit request (if any), and the proposed temporary SLA exception?

Next steps: when we have fallback approval we will enable the hosted routing, proceed with the remaining kernel updates on off-hours, and follow up with a post-mortem and a permanent kernel-profile change for Private.

Alex, Samir — let me know if we have permission to start the fallback now. If we don't get approval in 20 minutes we'll keep the reduced concurrency and continue rolling kernel patches.

Regards,
